A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Eyes-on-Me research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original attack-success, transferability, ablation, and defense experiments in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds reranker, fluency-proxy, and payload-length evaluations.

M1.justification: The attractor/payload decomposition, correlated-head attention objective, and HotFlip procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 move from Appendix F to G. The stronger fluency model is tested as an alternative configuration, without replacing the core method.

E1.justification: The three QA datasets and existing attack tasks remain. Section 5.4 adds a deployment scenario with BCE and Qwen cross-encoder rerankers between retrieval and generation.

E2.justification: GCG, Phantom/MCG, AutoDAN, and LLM-Gen remain the evaluated attack baselines. The new reranker table uses this existing comparator set, abbreviating LLM-Gen as LLM. Rerankers are evaluation targets rather than new competing attacks.

E3.justification: v3 adds top-100 retrieval followed by top-5 reranking with SR@5/MRR, a GPT-2 versus Qwen2.5-3B fluency-proxy comparison, and a 15–75-token payload-length sweep with fixed attractors. The main evaluation protocol remains. BCE's reported size changes from 110M to 279M for the same named model, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The generalization and robustness evidence is substantially revised: v3 adds reranker testing, stronger fluency-proxy testing, and focus-region-length ablations, distinct from the retained attractor-length analysis. It removes v2's detailed trigger-transfer matrix and base-method trigger-frequency analysis. The hybrid method's frequency analysis remains in Appendix H.

E5.justification: v2's reproducibility statement says random seeds were fixed where possible; v3 removes that disclosure. Neither version supplies repeated-run uncertainty intervals for attack success. The PDFs do not establish any change in actual run counts.

E6.justification: Table 1, model-transfer results, and Table 5 defense scores are unchanged. v3 adds reranker results, including 94.17% SR@5 for the hybrid on Qwen; reports 65.80% versus 76.92% ASR under different fluency proxies; and adds payload-length results spanning 41–67% ASR. Detailed trigger-transfer and base-frequency rows disappear. The newly stated 62% transfer average equals the mean of v2's off-diagonal entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, attention objective, and algorithmic mathematics remain unchanged. New Appendix F provides conceptual mechanistic explanations and explicitly distinguishes these from formal causal proofs; it adds no theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution (1) now explicitly claims up to 62% ASR without retraining, 'matching white-box baselines.' v2 claimed reuse without this comparison. The modular poisoning contribution and headline 57.8% result remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 replaces v2's emphasis on inconsistent trigger transfer with near-white-box performance framing and removes the mean-pooling limitation. It adds shared-attention/representation explanations in Appendix F, interprets reranker transfer through source-family specialization, and discusses fluency–efficacy tradeoffs and payload attention dilution.

D1.justification: The code pointer changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. Appendices B/C specify the added fluency proxy and rerankers and revise BCE's parameter count. v3 removes the NVIDIA H200 context for optimization times; most existing hyperparameters, dataset-subset information, and pseudocode remain.

R1.justification: New Appendix F adds Angell et al. (2026), Liang et al. (2026), and Zaree et al. (2025), connecting transferability to shared representations, order-level attention, and attention manipulation. The existing related-work section and central novelty positioning largely remain.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. v3 makes targeted wording changes, replaces the Ethics Statement with an Impact Statement, removes the separate limitations, LLM-usage, and reproducibility passages, and inserts appendices that shift Algorithms F→G and hybrid ablations G→H.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and repositioning figures and tables. v3 adds the reranker table, removes transfer and frequency panels, restructures ablation displays, redraws length/PCA plots, and changes Figure 2's illustrative city from Rio de Janeiro to Seoul.

improvement.justification: Reranker testing addresses an explicit v2 limitation, and the new ablations help characterize operating limits. However, v3 removes detailed transfer and base-frequency evidence and the mean-pooling caveat while strengthening transfer claims. Appendix I also compares a 75-token payload against a Table 1 baseline documented with roughly 60 tokens for the entire passage. Improved coverage and reduced auditability and comparison clarity prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
